title: Scout Selection: Best Fantasy team for Gameweek 4
body:
There are triple-ups on Chelsea and Liverpool in the best team for Gameweek 4 of Fantasy Premier League ahead of Saturday’s 13:30 BST deadline. Remember, you can pick this side if you are playing your Free Hit chip this week.

Both clubs have very favourable home matches at 15:00 BST on Saturday afternoon.

Chelsea trio Cole Palmer (£9.6m), Morgan Rogers (£7.6m) and Joao Pedro (£7.7m) are at home to promoted Hull City, while Liverpool’s Alisson (£5.5m), Dominik Szoboszlai (£7.0m) and Alexander Isak (£9.1m) are up against Fulham at Anfield.

There's a double-up on Arsenal, meanwhile, with Ezri Konsa (£4.4m) and Martin Odegaard (£6.6m) selected for the Gunners' trip to Sunderland on Saturday night.

Palmer is handed the armband, with Joao Pedro named as vice-captain.

Alisson (Liverpool) £5.5m

Liverpool's goalkeeper collected eight points at Ipswich Town in Gameweek 3, supplementing a clean sheet with one save point and one bonus point. With so much budget spent in attack, Alisson offers a £1.0m saving over Virgil van Dijk (£6.5m) if you're on a Free Hit chip and want to invest in the Reds' rearguard against Fulham.

Anan Khalaili (Crystal Palace) £5.0m

Crystal Palace’s new wing-back has collected defensive contribution (DC) points in both of his starts ahead of a favourable home match against promoted Ipswich. As evidenced by the two goals of his fellow wing-back Tyrick Mitchell (£4.5m), the Eagles’ wide defenders offer plenty of attacking threat under new boss Pierre Sage. 

Maxim De Cuyper (Brighton) £4.8m

Listed as a defender in Fantasy, De Cuyper has profited from a role as a left-sided midfielder for Brighton & Hove Albion recently, scoring once and supplying two assists. He visits a Coventry City side who have yet to score this season, suggesting a clean sheet could also be on the cards.

Ezri Konsa (Arsenal) £4.4m

The centre-back made an immediate impact on his full debut for Arsenal, collecting two DC points in their win over Chelsea last weekend. Konsa's very kind price has made him the top target in defence this Gameweek, with over 361,000 transfers in. 

Cole Palmer (Chelsea) £9.6m

Palmer's two goals (including a penalty) as a substitute in Chelsea's EFL Cup win over Leeds United in midweek served another reminder he is back to his best under new manager Xabi Alonso. His nine shots in the box are more than twice the four of Rogers, while his classification as a midfielder in Fantasy earns him the captaincy over Joao Pedro; whereas midfielders earn five points for a goal and one point for a clean sheet, forwards earn four points for a goal and no points for a clean sheet. 

Morgan Rogers (Chelsea) £7.6m

Along with Cody Gakpo (£7.2m), Rogers is one of only two midfielders or forwards who have produced an attacking return (a goal or an assist) in each of the first three Gameweeks. Having supplied FOUR assists against Leeds off the bench in the EFL Cup in midweek, Rogers is now the second most-bought player in Gameweek 4, with 580,000+ managers bringing him in for the Hull encounter.

Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool) £7.0m

The Hungarian is the second most-sold player in Gameweek 4, with 366,000+ managers parting ways with the Liverpool midfielder. Szoboszlai's goal against Atletico Madrid in the UEFA Champions League in midweek indicates many of those backers could regret their decision for the Reds' match against Fulham, while his appeal is boosted further by his dominance of dead-ball duties - he has taken all 12 of Liverpool's corners, all six of their free-kicks and their only penalty this season.

Martin Odegaard (Arsenal) £6.6m

Arsenal's captain looks back to his best after a frustrating injury-plagued 2025/26. Having scored and earned double-figure hauls in two of the first three Gameweeks, Odegaard extended that form by scoring the decisive goal in a 1-0 win at Napoli in the UEFA Champions League in midweek.

Watch: Experts reveal their GW4 teams
Erling Haaland (Man City) £15.5m

Manchester City's talisman was another standout performer in Europe in midweek, scoring both their goals in a 2-0 win at Porto. Nonetheless, a visit to rivals Manchester United does dent Haaland's captaincy potential for once, particularly when Chelsea and Liverpool have such strong home fixtures. 

Alexander Isak (Liverpool) £9.1m

Three goals in his last two league outings have taken Isak on to 23 points, just one behind Haaland in the forward standings. If you want to go against Palmer, Joao Pedro and Haaland with the captaincy, then Fulham's defensive numbers look very encouraging for Liverpool's attackers. The Cottagers have conceded 14 big chances (a situation where a player is expected to score) over the first three Gameweeks, at least three more than any other side. 

Joao Pedro (Chelsea) £7.7m

Chelsea's Brazilian is the most-owned player in Fantasy, with an ownership of 72.5 per cent only likely to keep growing ahead of a great long-term schedule. There is very little to separate Joao Pedro and Palmer so far - they are level on 21 points and have both created six chances, while Palmer just edges it for shots in the box, by nine to eight.
